harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a 3-member etcd (v3.5.17) cluster on node1/node2/node3 (RHEL 7.9) using systemd-managed etcd with static bootstrap over TCP 2379/2380 (firewalld opened). Fixed a stale system clock on all nodes (chrony resync) that had been blocking TLS downloads. Verified cross-node replication, availability during a single-member outage, and automatic catch-up when the member rejoined. Completed the mandatory sequential-restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed kernel boot_id and full cluster/quorum/data recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Diagnosed and fixed incorrect system clocks (Aug 26 vs actual Sep 8 2026) via chronyc burst+makestep on node1, node2, node3
Downloaded and installed etcd/etcdctl/etcdutl v3.5.17 binaries to /usr/local/bin on all three nodes
Created etcd system user/group and /var/lib/etcd data dir (0700, owned by etcd) plus /etc/etcd/etcd.conf per node with node-specific peer/client URLs and shared initial-cluster string
Installed systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/etcd.service on each node (Type=notify, User=etcd, EnvironmentFile)
Opened firewalld ports 2379/tcp and 2380/tcp permanently on all three nodes
Started etcd on all nodes to bootstrap a new 3-member cluster; confirmed member list and endpoint health all true
Wrote a key via node1 and confirmed it was readable from node2 and node3 (replication proof)
Stopped etcd on node3, wrote/read a key against node1/node2 to prove continued availability with one member down, confirmed leader election held with 2/3 quorum
Restarted etcd on node3 and confirmed it caught up to the same raft applied index and had the key written during its outage
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster health baseline for all three nodes
Sequentially restarted node1, then node2, then node3 via systemctl reboot, polling each until exec access returned
Confirmed each node's kernel boot_id changed after its restart, that its clock remained correct, and that etcd came back active/enabled
After each node's restart, verified full 3-node endpoint health, member list, and presence of all previously-written keys before moving to the next node
Final end-to-end write from node3 and read from node1 confirmed the cluster fully functional after all three restarts

evidence.requirement: 3-member etcd cluster formed across node1/node2/node3
evidence.summary: etcdctl member list shows node1, node2, node3 all status 'started' with correct peer/client addrs; endpoint health true for all three.

evidence.requirement: Key written through one member is readable from the others
evidence.summary: Wrote /bench/hello on node1 (10.100.13.10:2379); read back identical value from node2 (10.100.13.11:2379) and node3 (10.100.13.12:2379).

evidence.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads/writes while one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: Stopped etcd on node3; with only node1/node2 up, a write to /bench/during-outage succeeded (leader elected on node2) and was immediately readable from node2.

evidence.requirement: Unavailable member catches up when it returns
evidence.summary: Restarted etcd on node3; it read back /bench/during-outage and /bench/hello, and endpoint status showed identical raft term/applied index (16) across all three members.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id b35fad86... on node1 prior to restart, alongside full-cluster health confirmation.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued on node1; command returned 'reboot acknowledgement issued' before the SSH connection was closed by the remote host.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id on node1 is 39b627c8..., differing from the pre-restart b35fad86..., with a new uptime -s boot timestamp.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: recovered service/data/cluster state
evidence.summary: etcd active/enabled after reboot; full 3-node endpoint health true, member list intact, and /bench/hello and /bench/during-outage both readable from node1.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged then connection closed; new boot_id 6e7d7428... confirmed distinct from prior session; post-restart etcd active, all 3 endpoints healthy, and both test keys readable from node2.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged then connection closed; new boot_id b0462986... confirmed distinct; post-restart etcd active, all 3 endpoints healthy, member list intact, and both test keys readable from node3.

evidence.requirement: Cluster fully functional after all three sequential restarts
evidence.summary: After all nodes had been restarted, wrote /bench/post-restart from node3 and read it back successfully from node1, confirming end-to-end write/replication path still works.
